integrity: The proof is affine-invariant and splits every possible plane by the sign pattern of its barycentric coefficient vector. The triangular sign pattern is solved directly; the quadrilateral sign pattern is reduced to two exact rational centroid equations and an exact polynomial resultant, replayed by the packaged symbolic checker. Zero-coefficient boundary cases are handled separately.
scientific_limitations: The classification is proved only for three-dimensional tetrahedra and only for hyperplane sections through the tetrahedron centroid. It does not classify arbitrary simplex dimensions, arbitrary interior base points, or general convex bodies. A residual originality risk remains because an equivalent elementary simplex statement may exist under older terminology.
title: Exactly seven centroidal hyperplane sections of every tetrahedron
